name: bittle_list_capabilities
description: List what the Bittle robot can do right now: every callable skill (postures, gaits, behaviors), every controllable joint with its SAFE angle range, and whether real hardware is currently reachable. Call this FIRST before any movement command — skill names and joint limits are hardware-specific and guessing them gets the command rejected. Angle ranges returned here are the effective safe limits (firmware range intersected with the wire encoding's range); commanding outside them is clamped, not honoured.

name: bittle_status
description: Current robot state: E-stop status, rate-limit headroom, active target (sim or real), connection state and last known joint angles. Use this to check whether a previous command actually took effect, or to find out why commands are being refused (a latched E-stop returns 'engaged' here and blocks all motion until cleared by a human).

target.description: Which target to report on. Defaults to 'sim'.

name: bittle_do_skill
description: Run a named Bittle skill — a posture (sit, balance, rest), a behavior (hi, pushup, stretch) or a gait (wkF, trF). Skill names must come from bittle_list_capabilities; unknown names are REJECTED rather than ignored. Gaits physically drive the robot across whatever surface it is on, so they additionally require ack_locomotion=true, which you should only set once you have confirmed with the user that the area is clear. Defaults to the simulator: set target='real' only when the user has explicitly asked to move the physical robot.

skill.description: Skill name from bittle_list_capabilities, e.g. 'sit', 'balance', 'hi', 'wkF'. The leading 'k' is optional.

target.description: 'sim' (default, safe) or 'real' (physical servos). Only use 'real' on explicit user instruction.

ack_locomotion.description: Set true ONLY for gaits, and only after confirming the robot has clear space to move. Walking on a table means walking off it.

name: bittle_move_joints
description: Set specific joint angles, in degrees. Accepts joint indices or names ('head', 'knee_front_left') mapped to angles. Angles outside a joint's safe range are CLAMPED and the response reports every adjustment — read that back rather than assuming your requested angle was applied. Joints move simultaneously by default, which is safer than sequential motion because sequential motion passes through intermediate poses you did not request. Prefer bittle_do_skill for anything a named skill already covers; hand-built poses are for cases no skill fits.

angles.description: Map of joint index or name to angle in degrees, e.g. {"head": 20, "12": 60}. Only populated joints are accepted; slots 4-7 do not exist on Bittle.

target.description: 'sim' (default, safe) or 'real'. Only use 'real' on explicit user instruction.

simultaneous.description: Move all joints together (default true). Set false only when a joint must lead deliberately.

name: bittle_estop
description: EMERGENCY STOP. Immediately releases servo torque on every target and latches a block on all further motion until a human clears it. Call this the moment something looks wrong — a servo straining, the robot near an edge, or the user saying stop. It is never rate-limited and never refused. Be aware the robot goes limp, so a standing robot will drop into a crouch; that is the correct trade against a stalling servo.

reason.description: Short note on why the stop was triggered, for the operator log.

name: bittle_execute_sequence
description: Execute a choreographed multi-frame sequence of joint angles with per-frame delays and speeds. Dry-run pre-flight validated before execution.

steps.description: Array of keyframe step objects with 'type' ('move'|'pause'), 'angles' ({joint: deg}), 'delay_ms', 'speed_deg_per_step'

target.description: 'sim' (default, safe) or 'real'. Only use 'real' on explicit user instruction.

name: bittle_save_moveset
description: Save a named multi-frame moveset to the robot library for future replay, composition, or sharing.

name.description: Unique identifier for the moveset, e.g. 'cat_stalk'

frames.description: Array of keyframe dicts with 'angles' ({joint: deg}), 'delay_ms', 'speed_deg_per_step'

source_primitives.description: Optional list of primitive names used to build this moveset

name: bittle_list_primitives
description: List available motion primitives (per-limb clips). Each primitive targets a specific joint group and can be snapped together into full moves.

group.description: Filter by joint group. Omit to list all primitives.

name: bittle_compose_move
description: Compose a new moveset by snapping named primitives together. Modes: sequential (end-to-end), parallel (merge joint-disjoint into simultaneous frames), blend (sequential with smooth interpolation frames).

name.description: Unique name for the composed moveset

primitives.description: Ordered list of primitive names to compose

mode.description: Composition mode. sequential=end-to-end, parallel=simultaneous (rejects collisions), blend=interpolated transitions

name: bittle_iterate_move
description: Tweak an existing moveset's parameters: scale delays, speeds, apply angle offsets to specific joints, swap primitives, or insert/remove frames.

name.description: Name of moveset to iterate on

adjustments.description: Adjustment dict: delay_scale (float), speed_scale (float), angle_offsets ({joint:offset}), swap_primitive ({old,new}), insert_frame ({index,frame}), remove_frame (int)

name: bittle_evaluate_move
description: Dry-run evaluate and score a moveset without executing. Returns smoothness score (0-100), duration estimate, max delta, and reversal count.

name.description: Moveset name to evaluate from library

frames.description: Or provide raw frames to evaluate inline

name: bittle_list_library
description: List all saved movesets in the robot library (built-in + user-created + GLM-composed).

name: bittle_load_moveset
description: Load a previously saved moveset by name from the library for inspection, replay, or further iteration.
